answer.evidence: The silhouette is 32px wide from row 12 to 31. Rows 12-20 form a top band: a light back rim at row 12, a mid-tone panel with a row of indicator lights in rows 14-18, and a light front-edge line at row 20 (L=172). Row 21 is a dark shadow line (L=38) directly under it. Below that, rows 21-31 are the south face, with drawer or panel recesses in rows 22-28 and a dark base in rows 29-31, about 11 rows in all. The thin antennas in rows 7-11 are small details. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a grey metal control console with four small indicator posts on top and a row of knobs and slots on the front. The measured facts are 12 colours per tile (the references range from 10 to 20 where measurable), 4% flat-fill coverage and 14 distinct colours in total. That total is equal to the bench and lamp but far below the stall (40) and well (38). The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans tinted (bluish-grey) rather than black, which is the right treatment. The body of the console reads as roughly 3 lightness steps: a light top edge, a mid grey face and a dark base. It has little per-element shading or grain, and the knobs and buttons are tiny. Next to the stall and well, which carry 5-6 steps with clump and tile texture, it looks flatter and thinner. It is clean and not a sticker, but it is shallower than the Beodeul standard for a prop of this size.

styleAnswer.evidence: The console is a 2-tile grey-blue metal box with a panel face, knob/button rows and small indicator posts on top. It uses about 4 lightness steps on the casing, against about 5 on the Beodeul props. The measured facts support it: 12 distinct colours per tile is above the hedge (10) and in line with the stall and well (17-20). Flat-fill coverage is only 4%, and the grid lines, knobs and panel segments break up the surface. 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans toward the casing's tinted dark tone rather than a black sticker line. At 14 total colours it is no more limited than the bench and lamp (14 each), though it is a little less textured than the stall and well. A careful artist would accept it beside the references.

Measured facts: 12 colours per tile, above the hedge's 10 and below the stall's 17 and the well's 20. 4% flat-fill coverage is low, and its 14 distinct colours match the bench and lamp, though well below the stall (40) and well (38). 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark version of the body colour rather than a black sticker line.
